evals.prompt: We pushed a new policy.yml to the security policy project an hour ago and now no project in the group runs SAST or secret detection any more.
evals.expected_output: Treat whole-document silent rejection as the leading hypothesis; verify via GraphQL loaded policies and schema validation at the instance version tag before anything else.
assertions: Identifies the empty projects.including list and string project id in the fixture as schema/semantic problems
Explains that one invalid entry disables every policy in the document
Proposes linting/schema validation in the delivery pipeline as prevention
Does not suggest editing policies in the UI as the fix when a delivery mechanism owns them

evals.prompt: Dependency scanning gradle-resolution fails in about 40 Android projects since we switched to the v2 template. Log: 'Gradle requires at least JVM runtime version 21. You are currently using 17'.
evals.expected_output: Classify as project-owned daemon JVM requirement, give the gradle-daemon-jvm.properties fix with wrapper prerequisite, verify resolution image ships the JDK, and recommend a survey to size the problem.
assertions: Assigns ownership to the project, with platform providing a multi-JDK resolution image
Mentions toolchainVersion and the Gradle wrapper minimum version
Does not recommend disabling dependency scanning or reverting to v1 as the primary fix
Suggests scripts/survey_failed_jobs.py to count affected projects

evals.prompt: Team asks for an exception: ignore all findings for CVE-* in their repo for a year because the scanner is noisy.
evals.expected_output: Reject as written; propose narrowest workable exceptions (specific identifiers or paths) with mandatory metadata and expiry within organisation maximum, risk owner approval.
assertions: Rejects the wildcard identifier
Requires justification, owner, ticket and an expiry not exceeding policy maximum
Offers a concrete narrower alternative
Notes that auto-dismissal happens at the next default-branch ingestion and is not reverted automatically on removal

evals.prompt: A developer says GitLab flags 5000 dependency issues in their Android app while SonarQube found nothing. Are these real? Write a reply.
evals.expected_output: Evidence-based reply: different tool categories (SAST vs SCA), group by manifest/configuration, separate shipped vs build-only dependencies, give a prioritised next step; no overclaiming reachability.
assertions: Explains SCA versus SAST without dismissing the developer
Recommends grouping findings by location and configuration before judging
Does not claim all findings are false positives or all are exploitable
Keeps the reply concise and actionable

evals.prompt: Design central SAST, secret detection and dependency scanning enforcement for ~2000 projects on GitLab 18.8 self-managed. Findings must not block yet, but we want to introduce blocking later per business unit.
evals.expected_output: Group-level security policy project linkage, scan execution policies with MR and default-branch rules, tags, ignore_default_before_after_script, phased modes (scan -> warn -> block) with fail-closed gates later, exceptions model, version-checked schema, staged rollout and surveys.
assertions: Verifies features against the 18.8 schema rather than latest docs
Keeps policy limits (5 per type, action maxProperties) in mind
Includes a non-production verification and rollback plan
Maps controls to at least one recognised standard without inventing clause text

evals.prompt: Policy jobs in a newly created project stay pending forever with 'This job is stuck because the project doesn't have any runners online assigned to it'.
evals.expected_output: Compare job tag_list with available runners; most likely policy actions lack required tags; fix centrally by adding tags to every action; also check project linkage for new projects.
assertions: Checks the job tag_list before blaming runner capacity
Places the fix in the policy actions, not in the project's .gitlab-ci.yml
Mentions re-running jobs after the fix because pending jobs do not pick up policy changes

evals.prompt: We removed a path exception yesterday but the vulnerabilities are still dismissed and a merge request is still blocked by the security gate after the finding was dismissed.
evals.expected_output: Explain that GitLab does not revert auto-dismissals and that override documents may need a DIRECT resync; MR approval rules are snapshotted; propose approve/re-evaluate/recreate MR and an automation to re-open dismissed findings.
assertions: Distinguishes the two symptoms
Flags mergeRequestResyncSecurityPolicies as experimental and unverified if suggested
Labels any resync mutation as a write operation requiring approval
